    // The distance from the query offset to the feature point of the k-th cell of
    // the 3x3x3 neighbourhood, k counted x fastest then y then z.
    WorleyNeighbour3D(self: WorleyNoise3D, i: Integer, j: Integer, k: Integer, fx: Number, fy: Number, fz: Number, n: Integer): Number {
        var dx = n % 3 - 1;
        var dy = n / 3 % 3 - 1;
        var dz = n / 9 - 1;
        var feature = FeatureOffset3D(self.Seed, i + dx, j + dy, k + dz, self.Jitter);
        var offset = Vector3D(dx.ToNumber + feature.X - fx,
                              dy.ToNumber + feature.Y - fy,
                              dz.ToNumber + feature.Z - fz);
        return WorleyLength(offset, self.Distance);
    }

    // The chosen combination of the two nearest feature distances. Non-negative.
    Eval(self: WorleyNoise3D, p: Point3D): Number {
        var x = p.X * self.Frequency;
        var y = p.Y * self.Frequency;
        var z = p.Z * self.Frequency;
        var i = x.Floor.ToInteger;
        var j = y.Floor.ToInteger;
        var k = z.Floor.ToInteger;
        var fx = x - x.Floor;
        var fy = y - y.Floor;
        var fz = z - z.Floor;
        var distances = 27.MapRange(n => self.WorleyNeighbour3D(i, j, k, fx, fy, fz, n));
        var f1 = NearestDistance(distances);
        return WorleyCombine(f1, SecondNearestDistance(distances, f1), self.Feature);
    }

    //==
    // # Gabor noise
    //
    // Sparse convolution: one Gabor kernel — a Gaussian envelope times a plane
    // wave — per lattice cell, summed over the neighbourhood. Bandwidth is the
    // envelope's decay rate, so a large bandwidth localizes each kernel and
    // widens the spectrum; Anisotropy blends each kernel's own random orientation
    // (0) toward the field's stated one (1).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabor_filter

    // One cell's kernel, evaluated at the query offset.
    GaborKernel2D(self: GaborNoise2D, i: Integer, j: Integer, fx: Number, fy: Number, k: Integer): Number {
        var dx = k % 3 - 1;
        var dy = k / 3 - 1;
        var ci = i + dx;
        var cj = j + dy;
        var h = LatticeHash(self.Seed, ci, cj);
        var impulse = FeatureOffset2D(self.Seed, ci, cj, 1.0);
        var vx = dx.ToNumber + impulse.X - fx;
        var vy = dy.ToNumber + impulse.Y - fy;
        var envelope = (-Number.Pi * self.Bandwidth * (vx * vx + vy * vy)).Exp;
        // The kernel's wave direction: its own random orientation dragged toward
        // the field's by Anisotropy.
        var own = HashToUnit(NoiseMix(h)).Turns;
        var direction = Vector2D(own.Cos.Lerp(self.Orientation.Cos, self.Anisotropy),
                                 own.Sin.Lerp(self.Orientation.Sin, self.Anisotropy)).Normalize;
        var phase = Angle((vx * direction.X + vy * direction.Y) * Number.Tau);
        return HashToSigned(h) * envelope * phase.Cos;
    }

    // The summed kernel response over the 3x3 neighbourhood.
    Eval(self: GaborNoise2D, p: Point2D): Number {
        var x = p.X * self.Frequency;
        var y = p.Y * self.Frequency;
        var i = x.Floor.ToInteger;
        var j = y.Floor.ToInteger;
        var fx = x - x.Floor;
        var fy = y - y.Floor;
        return 9.MapRange(k => self.GaborKernel2D(i, j, fx, fy, k)).Reduce(0.0, (acc, v) => acc + v);
    }

    // One cell's kernel in three dimensions.
    GaborKernel3D(self: GaborNoise3D, i: Integer, j: Integer, k: Integer, fx: Number, fy: Number, fz: Number, n: Integer): Number {
        var dx = n % 3 - 1;
        var dy = n / 3 % 3 - 1;
        var dz = n / 9 - 1;
        var ci = i + dx;
        var cj = j + dy;
        var ck = k + dz;
        var h = LatticeHash(self.Seed, ci, cj, ck);
        var impulse = FeatureOffset3D(self.Seed, ci, cj, ck, 1.0);
        var v = Vector3D(dx.ToNumber + impulse.X - fx,
                         dy.ToNumber + impulse.Y - fy,
                         dz.ToNumber + impulse.Z - fz);
        var envelope = (-Number.Pi * self.Bandwidth * v.LengthSquared).Exp;
        var own = LatticeGradient3D(self.Seed, ck, ci, cj);
        var direction = own.Lerp(self.Direction.Vector, self.Anisotropy).Normalize;
        var phase = Angle(v.Dot(direction) * Number.Tau);
        return HashToSigned(h) * envelope * phase.Cos;
    }

    // The summed kernel response over the 3x3x3 neighbourhood.
    Eval(self: GaborNoise3D, p: Point3D): Number {
        var x = p.X * self.Frequency;
        var y = p.Y * self.Frequency;
        var z = p.Z * self.Frequency;
        var i = x.Floor.ToInteger;
        var j = y.Floor.ToInteger;
        var k = z.Floor.ToInteger;
        var fx = x - x.Floor;
        var fy = y - y.Floor;
        var fz = z - z.Floor;
        return 27.MapRange(n => self.GaborKernel3D(i, j, k, fx, fy, fz, n)).Reduce(0.0, (acc, v) => acc + v);
    }

    //==
    // # Fractal noise evaluation
    //
    // The `Eval` bodies for the multi-octave sums of `noise.types.plato`.
    // Every one is the same shape: sample the Basis noise Octaves times, the k-th
    // octave at Frequency * Lacunarity^k with weight Gain^k, and divide by the total
    // weight so the result keeps the basis's own range rather than growing with the
    // octave count.
    //
    // The per-octave seed is offset by the octave index. Reusing one seed across
    // octaves would make every layer the SAME field at different scales, which is
    // visible as a self-similar grid rather than as detail.
    //
    // Octaves is a runtime count, so each sum is `MapRange` over the octave indices
    // followed by `Reduce` — the vocabulary has no loop, and recursion would rebuild
    // the weights at every level.

    //==
    // # Weights
    //
    // Shared by all three families: the k-th octave's amplitude, and the total
    // that normalizes the sum. With Gain < 1 the total converges to
    // 1 / (1 - Gain), so a high octave count costs weight but not range.

    // The amplitude of octave k: gain raised to the octave index.
    OctaveWeight(gain: Number, k: Integer): Number
        => gain.Pow(k.ToNumber);

    // The sum of the octave amplitudes, which every fractal sum divides by.
    // Returns one for a zero octave count so the division is still defined.
    TotalWeight(gain: Number, octaves: Integer): Number {
        var total = octaves.MapRange(k => OctaveWeight(gain, k)).Reduce(0.0, (acc, w) => acc + w);
        return total <= 0.0 ? 1.0 : total;
    }

    //==
    // # Fractional Brownian motion
    //
    // The plain weighted sum: signed, and nominally back in [-1, 1] after
    // normalization. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fractional_Brownian_motion

    // The signed contribution of octave k.
    FbmOctave(basis: NoiseBasis, seed: Integer, frequency: Number, lacunarity: Number, gain: Number, p: Point2D, k: Integer): Number
        => BasisValue2D(basis, seed + k, frequency * lacunarity.Pow(k.ToNumber), p)
           * OctaveWeight(gain, k);

    // The signed contribution of octave k.
    FbmOctave(basis: NoiseBasis, seed: Integer, frequency: Number, lacunarity: Number, gain: Number, p: Point3D, k: Integer): Number
        => BasisValue3D(basis, seed + k, frequency * lacunarity.Pow(k.ToNumber), p)
           * OctaveWeight(gain, k);
